components: a small left loop rising into the crown
a large right loop curling inward and running out into a tail
a hooked lower bowl hanging from the tail
strokeOrder: circle the small left loop and climb into the crown
without lifting, sweep through the large right loop, curl inward, and run out along the tail
without lifting, come back along the tail to the lower bowl, sweep around its broad curl, and turn inward into the hook — and only now lift
strokeOrderNote: one stroke — the manual numbers three movements; native writers draw them without lifting, and this ductus follows them in order, coming back along the tail into the hooked lower bowl; cited to Radhakrishnan, Tamil Script Learners Manual, Module 15 and Appendix I Frame 15, ஓ

strokeOrderSource.citation: Sankaran Radhakrishnan, Tamil Script Learners Manual, Module 15, ஓ, with Appendix I: Hand-movements, Frame 15 (University of Texas at Austin), p. 196
strokeOrderSource.variation: Module 15 identifies ஓ as long o. Appendix I Frame 15 numbers three movements: the small left loop, the large right loop, and the hooked lower bowl. Native writers draw them as one continuous stroke, and this ductus follows the three movements in order without lifting: the large loop ends at the tip of the tail, and the bundled Noto Sans Tamil outline joins the top of the hooked lower bowl to that tail, so the pen comes back along the tail before sweeping around the bowl. In HP Labs India's online Tamil handwriting data (the LipiTk 4.0 Tamil isolated-character recognizer, trained on hpl-tamil-iso-char), 97% of the 29 stored prototypes of ஓ are a single pen-down stroke. Tamil handwriting varies by school; this is one attested order fitted to the bundled Noto Sans Tamil outline.

notes: Independent long ō opens words such as ஓடு (ōṭu, run). Frame 15's three movements are one continuous stroke, the same family as short ஒ: the small left loop, the large right loop and its tail, then back along the tail into the larger hooked lower bowl.
